title: What If the Ground Under Your Street Opened Up?

scenes.text: What if the ground under your street just opened up? In Guatemala City, it did.
In 2010, after rain from Tropical Storm Agatha, a hole opened in downtown Guatemala City overnight.
Estimates put it around 65 feet across and at least 100 feet deep, a ten-story drop.
It swallowed a three-story building and electricity poles. A security guard was listed as missing.
Geologists suspected leaking sewer or water lines had been washing the soil away underneath.
The street looked solid until the moment it wasn't. Water can quietly hollow out the ground below.
